newsitem.title: FRANCE: French court clears guerrilla extradition to Spain.
newsitem.headline: French court clears guerrilla extradition to Spain.

text.p: A French court on Wednesday approved the extradition of Basque guerrilla Idoia "Tigress" Lopez Riano to Spain to face a charge of attempting to kill the head of the Spanish Supreme Court, justice sources said.

The Paris appeals court put off decisions on the extradition of several other ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) guerrillas, including the group's former leaders Francisco "Pakito" Mugica Garmendia and Jose Maria Arregui Erostarbe.
A final decision on whether to hand over Lopez Riano, 32, now rests with the French government.
Nicknamed the Tigress, Lopez Riano is also wanted in Spain in connection with 23 murders, including those of 16 paramilitary civil guards.
She was detained in France three years ago and jailed for five years after being convicted on conspiracy and weapons charges.
The Paris court also authorised the extradition of ETA member Carlos Almorza Arietta.
But it put off to April 2 its ruling on Spain's requests for the extradition of Mugica Garmendia and Arregui Erostarbe.
Spain believes Mugica Garmendia, captured in France five years ago, was the top leader of ETA which has killed some 800 people in a three-decade campaign for a separate Basque state.
He is wanted in Spain on charges of conspiracy and despatching a car bomb to Madrid in 1991.
Arregui Erostarbe is wanted in Spain in connection with a parcel bomb which badly maimed the presiding judge of the anti-terrorist court Audiencia Nacional, Fernando de Mateo Lage, in 1990.
The hearing on the extradition of Julian "Pototo" Achurra Egurola, 37, was postponed to a later date after he asked to leave the courtroom because of health problems.

"Pototo", wanted in Spain for the 1986 murder of a policeman in Bilbao, was captured in France last July and jailed for three years last October after being convicted on conspiracy charges. He was said to be in charge of ETA logistics.
Arregui Erostarbe spoke in French to ask the court to reject Spain's extradition requests and to denounce Madrid's jailing of members of Herri Batasuna, the party regarded as ETA's political wing.
"The Spanish state jails leaders of a legal political party. You will become accomplices if you rule in favour (of extraditions)," he said.

The others ETA members in court stuck to the separatists' practice of refusing to speak either French or Spanish and requesting translators in the Euskera Basque language. Their requests were turned down.
